slides.h: Is the universe we live in the inside of a black hole?
b: Most versions of that are slogans. One is an exact solution of Einstein's equations — the Big Bang as an explosion inside a black hole, with a shock wave surrounding everything we can see.
The week's work does not ask whether it is true. It asks: could we ever tell?

slides.h: The prize was never proof — it was a real test, or a proof that none exists
b: Ideas about our universe sitting inside something larger are cheap, and nearly all are unfalsifiable.
This one has a genuine boundary, and a boundary might leave a mark on the sky. Either outcome converts an argument into knowledge.

slides.h: From the inside it looks exactly like an ordinary universe
b: We assumed an off-centre observer would see the expansion run faster one way than another. It does not — exactly, not approximately.
That test is dead permanently, and we killed it ourselves.

slides.h: One patch of sky — and nobody had computed what crossing the wall looks like
b: The only fingerprint is a single round region, tens of degrees across, in one direction.
My first answer was wrong in an embarrassing way: inside a black hole space and time swap roles, and I used a time direction as a distance.

slides.h: There is a setting where the model produces no signal at all
b: Two effects fight — the wall's motion brightens, the differing viewing epochs dim — and at one composition they cancel exactly.
A reviewer found it. My own check could not have: I took the signal's size without its sign, across six settings, and a cancellation lives in the gaps between samples.

slides.h: Survival teaches little; exclusion kills one version; untestable is a real result
b: Surviving means sitting within a fraction of a percent of the centre — a coincidence, not a confirmation.
Proving it untestable by light would convert an idea that sounds unfalsifiable into one proved so. That is worth more than a weak bound.

slides.h: The model can produce no signal at all without being wrong
b: Any claim that this is a test of black-hole cosmology has to survive that sentence first.
It was found by someone attacking my work, not by me — which is why this is a state of play and not a result.
